newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares continue to fall on unrest.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares continue to fall on unrest.

text.p: Shares prices on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange opened lower on Sunday morning, after dropping sharply last week in response to violent clashes between Israeli soldiers and Palestinians.
The benchmark Mishtanim Index of top 100 shares opened down 0.54 percent or 1.01 points at 187.61 while the Maof 25 Index was off 0.53 percent at 196.44.

There was supply of 45.5 million shekels, a low figure, against demand of 21 million shekels, traders said. However, nearly all the demand was for Teva Pharmaceutical Industries , whose shares traded on Nasdaq rose nearly five percent on Friday.
Although the West Bank and Gaza were calmer over the weekend, the market continues to be shadowed by political uncertainty, Ron Weisberg of IBI Investment House said.
"There is already a small change in trend," Weisberg said, predicting share prices would likely continue lower for the next day or two before correcting.

The Mishtanim fell four percent on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend, in response to the violence that has killed nearly 70 people and raised concerns about the future of Middle East peace.
The Tel Aviv bourse will close two hours early on Sunday and throughout the week due to the Jewish holiday of Succoth. Normal trading hours will resume on October 6.
